Squamous carcinoma originates in the urinary bladder; association with schistosomiasis does not establish infection in every case.

Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, outside the axes; visceral smooth muscle origin does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma involves skin and is a lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm; lymphoma also requires the immune mechanism axis.
Neurodevelopmental disease with aldosteronism; ventricular hypertrophy occurs in 80-99%, and conduction defects in 30-79%. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Lacrimal aplasia, hearing impairment and dental defects define the syndrome; thumb phalanx duplication occurs in 2/2 reported patients.
Pulmonary dysmaturity syndrome is a chronic lung disorder of premature infants.
Water-triggered inducible urticaria affects skin; its uncertain mechanism does not establish an autoimmune or allergic disease.
Combined open brain and spinal cord malformation with failure of vertebral arch closure; anencephaly and spinal dysraphism are defining features.
Congenital bilateral enlargement of fingers directly affects the skeletal structures of the hands.
Congenital cardiac outflow malformation with a subpulmonary ventricular septal defect.
Infection directly inflames the abdominal peritoneum; underlying liver disease or gastrointestinal perforation does not establish additional organ involvement.
Defined as severe Hallermann-Streiff: ocular and craniofacial skeletal defects with skin atrophy; dental abnormalities are a major diagnostic feature.
APP-related Alzheimer disease causes cerebral neurodegeneration; vascular amyloid deposition alone does not establish functionally damaging vascular disease.
Inherited cone-rod retinal degeneration causes progressive visual dysfunction.
Renal tubular degeneration; seizures/intellectual disability, chronic pancreatitis and sensorineural hearing loss each occur in 2/5 patients. Hypertension is secondary.
Leucine metabolism defect; cerebral white matter abnormalities occur in 4/6 patients and developmental impairment in 30-79%. Hepatic and ocular findings are uncommon.
Defined by a pathogenic inflammatory response; no anatomical organ is shared across this broad umbrella.
Partial chromosome 9 gains commonly cause developmental disability and skeletal/digital abnormalities; cardiac and renal defects vary substantially by duplicated region.
Benign adipose neoplasm originates in the heart, epicardium or pericardium.
Fluid accumulation directly affects the macular retina and can impair central vision.
Eosinophilic inflammatory myofascial disease; fibrotic skin thickening occurs in 30-79%. Neurologic sensory loss and pleural abnormalities (30-79%) omitted by cap.
NEXN-related dilated cardiomyopathy directly damages cardiac muscle; hydrops and pleural effusions reflect heart failure rather than primary lung damage.
